<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Are there any working custom components?
same issue . happened today for DST in Sydney .
I need some help. my times have been off by an hour since DST. anyway I can solve this?

The update time has 2 possibilities:
- At midnight if the "calculated midnight" is before the actual midnight (00:00)
- After the "calculated midnight" if it is after the actual midnight.
I think if we change the first one to update at 00:01 this will ensure that the update happens after the DST change is applied. But first please let me know if the 'calculated midnight' in your case (the midnight sensor provided by this integration) is actually before 00:00

The DST change does not usually happens at midnight, instead it occurs between 2 & 3 am. i.e. it either moves forward  from 2am to 3am or backwards from 3am to 2am.

Therefore if the prayer time can be updated after 3 am  it will ensure it takes the new DST into consideration.

> The update time has 2 possibilities:
> 
>     * At midnight if the "calculated midnight" is before the actual midnight (00:00)
> 
>     * After the "calculated midnight" if it is after the actual midnight.
>       I think if we change the first one to update at 00:01 this will ensure that the update happens after the DST change is applied. But first please let me know if the 'calculated midnight' in your case (the midnight sensor provided by this integration) is actually before 00:00

It is actually after midnight (00:18:00)
The integration should run the calculation based on the system location so it runs after the daylight change. e.g. in Canada daylight change happens at 2:00 AM and this information is available in TZDATA

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daylight_saving_time_by_country
Thanks @B0ndo2 for the information. Looking at the above link I can see that the daylight change happens at 2 AM at most. So perhaps setting the update at 2:01 ensures all countries are covered.
Yes I believe it is safe to do it at 2:01 because that will always before Fajr. I hope to see the update before the next time change :-D

Salaam all. After reviewing the code, this seems to happen because the prayer times from aladhan.com API were fetched as hours and minutes only, and then converted to datetime timestamp using homeassistant's `dt_util.parse_datetime` function (looks like taken from Django). The problem is, the API already takes into account DST changes when giving the times, but the parsing function takes "current local timezone" when converting the hours into timestamp. When update happened at midnight during the day of DST change, the times had been used the DST hours while local timezone hasn't change -- thus the mismatch.

IMO, a "better" solution would be to fetch the times from the API on a different format. Aladhan.com API itself actually supports ISO8601 time format which already included date and timezone, unfortunately the PrayerTimesCalculator package this integration relies on hasn't support this format last time I checked. 

I agree with the previous comments that update on 2:01 AM should solve this problem. I have opened a PR #79881 for this issue implementing the proposed change. Would appreciate review and comments! Thank you!
A PR https://github.com/uchagani/prayer-times-calculator/pull/19 has been submitted to return prayer times in `iso8601` format. Hopefully this gets merged then we can update the integration in HASS.

DST change happens this morning, and my PR #79881 didn't fix the problem. I didn't dig deep enough and didn't get my code tested properly.

After some more digging it appears that AlAdhan.com API itself isn't always accurate. During DST change days, it returns the correct prayer time only if the given timestamp parameter falls after the time of DST change. Consider these two URLs:

A. http://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/1667717999?latitude=41.792434591&longitude=-87.5999356&method=2&iso8601=true
B. http://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/1667718000?latitude=41.792434591&longitude=-87.5999356&method=2&iso8601=true

They both fetch prayer times in the America/Chicago timezone with timestamps _one second apart_, A is for today (Nov 6th 2022) at 01:59:59AM UTC-5 (before DST ends), and B is today 01:00:00AM UTC-6 (when DST ends). 
For Fajr time, the response we got for A is `"Fajr":"2022-11-06T06:10:00-06:00"` while for B is `"Fajr":"2022-11-06T05:10:00-06:00"`

Even though they both were in UTC-6 timezone according to the ISO8601 format, they differ by 1 hour. The correct one is the time given by B (We can compare with http://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/1667631600?latitude=41.792434591&longitude=-87.5999356&method=2&iso8601=true, which shows that Fajr for yesterday Nov 5th 2022 02:00:00AM UTC-5 was on 06:09AM).

Meanwhile, the prayer_times_calculator library, which requires "date" on object construction, actually [converts the date into timestamp](https://github.com/uchagani/prayer-times-calculator/blob/master/prayer_times_calculator/pray_times_calculator.py#L107) that corresponds to the start of day (12AM) on the local timezone when calling the API. This is why the PR, or even manual restart on 6AM, didn't work: it doesn't matter when the prayer time is updated (1AM, 2AM, 6AM), the API call will be made with the timestamp parameter set to 12AM.

Looks like we will need another update on the prayer_times_calculator library. We can set the timestamp sent to the API to 6AM or so to ensure the timezone has changed. Alternatively, we can send the date without converting it to timestamp, as AlAdhan.com API actually accepts date in dd-mm-YYYY format as well. Given the date, it will use 6AM/7AM local time as the timestamp.
I had to manually restart HA today (one day after the time change) to get it to pick up the correct prayer times.

review_comments: If the update will be on a specific time this method is no longer required.

It's on a specific time (02:01 AM) but it can be on either the next day or the same day (handles if the integration was started/the server restarted/etc before 0200AM in the morning).

Do you think it is still good to handle this case?
The timings are fetched on initial setup or restart, you only need to schedule it the next day.

This is a corner case: suppose the restart/initialization happen at 01:00AM on Nov 6th, if schedule the next update for 02:01AM the next day (Nov 7th), then the timing will be incorrect for the entire day of Nov 6th (which happens to be the day when DST changes in some places).
DST change is happening in less than 2 weeks and this issue has been here for a long time. Do you have a fix?

> The timings are fetched on initial setup or restart, you only need to schedule it the next day.

This is a home automation system, a user shouldn't be concerned with having to manually restart the system to fix anything
